title: LAN, WAN, MAN, VLAN and VPN: where each one shows up

videos.script: A company has a head office and a branch in another city. Each office has its own network, and the two have to talk to each other. {{map}} That one sentence already holds most of this lesson. Each office's network is a LAN: yours, fast, cheap, and inside one building. {{lan}} What joins the two cities is a WAN: links you rent from a provider, through routers you will never log in to. {{wan}} Between those two sizes sits the MAN, a network the size of a city. {{man}} And a VLAN is a LAN cut out of a switch by configuration, which lesson 19 builds. {{vlan}} In the lab, the head office tries to reach the branch directly, and the provider refuses. It has no route to a private address. {{refused}} So you will build a VPN between the two routers, a WireGuard tunnel, typed at their prompts. The ping goes through. {{tunnel}} Then you will listen on the provider's cable while it does, and see what the provider can read. Two addresses, a port, and a size. Nothing else. {{wire}}
